items.text: Decision: don't adopt GitHub stacked PRs; use native sub-issues plus an ordered index in the parent issue.
This issue is a decision record that constrains #163's R5 split recipe; it implements nothing itself.
Stacked PRs don't raise or work around GitHub's 65,536-character body cap; the cap only triggers splitting.
Only real pain is losing plan→PR mapping; waiting, hand-rebasing, and blocked reviewers aren't pain points.
Stacks: public preview, needs gh-stack extension, strict bottom-up merge, merge-queue support still rolling out.
Assumes split layers are largely independent; code-dependent layers would strengthen the case for stacks.
R1: From the parent issue, all implementing PRs, their execution order, and open/closed state are discoverable.
R2: Split recipe files N sub-issues parented to the original issue, in execution order, via gh issue edit.
R3: Parent body has an authoritative '## Execution order' checklist listing sub-issues in order with their PRs.
R4: Each sub-issue gets a normal draft PR based on main with 'Closes #<sub-issue>'; no PR-to-PR targeting.
R5: No dependency on github/gh-stack, stacks REST/GraphQL, or stack webhooks; no gh extension install in bootstrap.
R6: Record revisit trigger: stacks GA AND (dependent layering routine OR wait/rebase costs seen); only reopens evaluation.
No bespoke stacking substitute; not implementing #163 R1/R5/R10 or fixing the wc -c defect.
Not changing dotfiles-repo PR practice; decision targets portable skills used in other repos.
Verify in #163 R5 work via tabletop benches (docs/research/*-bench/): order, checklist mismatch detected, gh-stack use fails.
